doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/brand-rename-mapping.md's own Governing rule section (lines 36-48, 'Where the original table was wrong') explicitly disavows freezing tokens purely because renaming them requires coordinated edits, and names LATTICE_* env vars, bin/lattice.js and bin/lattice-codex.js filenames, npm package names, and .lattice/ state-dir-class paths as examples of WRONGLY frozen coupling that must be RENAMED-with-read-both-compat under the corrected test. The bin/ row (line 117) was correctly updated to RENAMED (additive) plus a kept alias, matching the corrected rule. But the Mapping table below still marks several rows in the SAME wrongly-frozen class as plain FROZEN with unmodified coupling-style reasoning: .lattice/ state directory (line 124, reason is renaming would orphan existing state -- coupling, not evidence), .lattice-serve.json (line 125), .lattice-codex/ (line 126), packages/main npm package @lattice/core (line 130), root npm package lattice (line 131), lattice.config.json (line 132), LATTICE_* env prefix (line 133), managed-block markers (line 134), lattice.remote-push-approval.v1 schema literal (line 135). None of these tokens are among the 13 salt literals hashed into stored _hash fields (the table's own stated sole criterion for FROZEN at lines 22-34), so under the table's own corrected rule they should read RENAMED (additive) with a read-both compat path plus a kept-name safety note, the same treatment given to bin/, not plain FROZEN. This is a self-contradiction within the story's own governing decision doc: the prose narrative (Governing rule) and the verdict table (Mapping table) disagree about which rows the corrected test actually reclassifies. High severity because CHK-006 checklist context explicitly states these are exactly the surfaces requiring the corrected read-both-compat treatment, and a reader trusting the FROZEN verdict rows would conclude no rename/compat work is needed for these tokens, contradicting the story's own corrected instructions.

CHK-006 (the largest body of work in the story per its own context: 146 LATTICE_* env vars across 245 files, ~20104 lattice tokens under packages/, 1360 under scripts/, bin filenames, package name, code identifiers, plus a read-both compat requirement) has verificationIntent={happy:[],edge:[],adversarial:[]} and verificationEvidence=[] -- zero intent, zero evidence, confirmed by reading checklist.json directly. This is structural: checklist_update refuses verificationIntent once an item exists in DEV (PLAN-only field), and CHK-006 was added mid-DEV. Consequence: all 36 must-intents in the story belong to CHK-001..CHK-005; the single largest, highest-blast-radius deliverable (touching read-both compat semantics and the .githooks/pre-push arming string) carries none of the frameworks intent-to-evidence coverage discipline. Recommend either (a) an explicit, durable waiver-style acknowledgment of this framework gap for mid-DEV-added items, or (b) retroactively binding CHK-006s already-existing DEV evidence (residue-gate/audit-scan regressions, read-both compat tests) to explicit intentRefs so coverage accounting is not silently zero for the storys biggest checklist item.

scripts/verify-done-suite-green.mjs:29-30 hardcodes an absolute default log path INSIDE THE AUTHORING SESSIONS OWN SCRATCHPAD DIRECTORY (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-qipan-work-repo-Prooforstop/<session-uuid>/scratchpad/npmtest4.log) as the evidence for CHK-005:happy:0 (root DONE-blocking npm test suite is green). Two independent problems verified by direct execution: (1) NOT REPRODUCIBLE: the path is session/machine-local and outside the repo (git ls-files shows it is not tracked); a different reviewer, a fresh clone, or CI re-running the exact recorded command node scripts/verify-done-suite-green.mjs will get DONE-SUITE RED: no recorded suite log at ... not the recorded PASS, because that exact scratchpad path will not exist for them. (2) THE RECEIPT NEVER FINGERPRINTS THE LOG CONTENT: the verificationEvidence receipts outputDigest hashes only the verifiers own one-line stdout (DONE-SUITE GREEN: ...), never the log file bytes or path. I reproduced this directly: I replaced the 1544-line real log with a 6-line fabricated stub containing only a header plus a bare REAL_EXIT=0 line (no actual npm test output, no assertions run) and pointed the script at it via PROOF_OR_STOP_DONE_SUITE_LOG; the script printed the IDENTICAL verdict line DONE-SUITE GREEN: npm test exit=0, 0 failure lines and exited 0. So yes -- per the main agents own question -- this verifier CAN and DOES report GREEN while representing a suite that never actually ran, because nothing binds the receipts digest to the logs actual content, and the log itself lives outside storyFilesHash/materialHash coverage (its outside the git tree entirely). This is the single piece of evidence for the DONE-blocking suite is green -- the most consequential claim in the story per B-META-framework-audit:F-012s own framing -- and it currently rests on an unreproducible, content-unverified pointer.

scripts/verify-done-suite-green.mjs:66-69 excludes itself (SELF_REL) from its own staleness set with the stated rationale editing the checker cannot invalidate the suite result it reports. That rationale only holds if edits to this file are limited to detector LOGIC. But the files own content also contains the LOG default path (the pointer to the evidentiary source, line 30) -- changing WHICH file is treated as authoritative IS exactly the kind of edit that should force re-validation, and the self-exclusion specifically exempts it from ever tripping STALE. Separately, the staleness comparison is mtime-only (statSync(...).mtimeMs), not a content hash; git operations (checkout, merge, rebase, worktree creation) routinely produce mtimes that do not track content history, so is the log newer than every tracked source file is a weak, spoofable proxy for no source changed since this run, compounding finding B-cdf6:F-006 (log content itself is never hashed). Recommend: hash-pin the LOG path itself into the verifier (or require an explicit --log flag with no hardcoded default), and use content hashes rather than mtimes for the staleness comparison; if self-exclusion is kept, restrict it to a change-scoped diff of detector logic only, not blanket exclusion of the entire file including its data pointers.

doc-code-drift: docs/CLI.md:5 states proof-or-stop is the ONLY active product command ("proof-or-stop is the only active product command, pointing at the same set of project state, phase, gate, review, evidence, and handoff semantics"). This is factually wrong: bin/lattice.js exists in this repo, node bin/lattice.js --version resolves and prints the same version as node bin/proof-or-stop.js --version (both print Proof-or-Stop 0.3.252), because lattice is a deliberately retained deprecated alias per brand-rename-mapping.md line 117 (bin RENAMED additive, keep lattice as deprecated alias). It also directly contradicts the sibling decision doc docs/requirements/decisions/lifecycle-artifact-scope.md:218-220, which correctly states 'Both names are active entrypoints -- neither is the sole command -- and no additional runtime command is introduced' -- exactly the OQ-2 correction this story was supposed to land. docs/CLI.md was apparently never updated to match the OQ-2 resolution captured in lifecycle-artifact-scope.md, so the two governing docs about the SAME fact (is lattice or proof-or-stop the sole active command) now disagree. High severity: this is the precise doc-code-drift class this rename story exists to prevent, and it is a command/flow assertion, not prose.

CHK-002:adversarial:1s waiver (deferred_gate_evidence, pointing at B-META-framework-audit:F-005) is substantively HONEST -- I independently reproduced the underlying claim rather than trusting the main agents self-report. I built a throwaway git worktree of PRISTINE main (pre-B-cdf6, package name still lattice), ran npm --prefix packages/main run build plus npm --prefix packages/utils run build, then node bin/lattice.js init --profile codex --asset-mode full into a fresh scratch dir, and confirmed .lattice-codex/agents/lattice-implementer.md is written with the modular marker (<!-- proofbound:modular-role-body:v1 -->, 10898 bytes for that role). Running node bin/lattice-codex.js verify_codex against that fresh project independently reproduces the failure: Codex agent asset resolution reports assets absent=1 matches-runtime=12 stale=5, and Codex agents mirror: missing .claude/agents or .lattice-codex/agents is a HARD FAILURE on a project this rename never touched. This corroborates F-005s core claim (init writes modular, codex-adapter-checks.ts:387 expects legacy-full-context, pre-existing and unrelated to B-cdf6). One caveat for the record: F-005/F-012 in B-META-framework-audit/findings.json are both self-logged by agent:main-agent with evidenceState:verified based on the main agents own probe -- my repro above is the FIRST actually-independent verification of F-005s pre-existence claim; F-012s claim (270s receipt-executor timeout forces an audited escape for the DONE-suite intent) I did not independently reproduce (would require re-running the 270s+ timeout scenario), so treat F-012 as corroborated only by internal consistency with validation-executor.ts:43s documented constant, not by an independent repro.

doc-code-drift: docs/CLI.md's compatibility note (added by commit 5041d058e7, replacing the removed Deprecated bin aliases table) says 'see CHANGELOG.md for the alias inventory'. CHANGELOG.md contains no such inventory: grep -n bin/lattice.js CHANGELOG.md returns exactly one hit, a single unrelated historical verification-step mention from an older story (line 534, node bin/lattice.js tool_status --format=json), not a table or list of the three retained aliases (bin/lattice.js -> bin/proof-or-stop.js, bin/lattice-codex.js -> bin/proof-or-stop-codex.js, npm bin lattice -> npm bin proof-or-stop). The removed table WAS that inventory; deleting it while leaving a pointer to a document that never held (and does not now hold) an equivalent inventory means a user who needs to know what deprecated entrypoints exist and what they map to has nowhere to look -- brand-rename-mapping.md's row 117 documents the retention rationale but not a user-facing alias-to-canonical mapping table either. Medium severity: this is information loss from the table removal (matching the review-lane concern about whether the removal cost a user something they need), not a broken command, but the pointer itself is also a docs lie because the referenced location does not contain what is promised.
